Toreador:

[!malk]

Destroy the others.

Be last and get two.

perfect clarity;
no longer the laughingstock:
you will not deflect.

intercept combat?
rotschreck is the way to lose -
go forward instead.

second round combat,

too much to support.

sorcerors supreme?
thaumaturgy is crappy...
potence it is not.

bruise and bleed Tremere,
three cross-purpose disciplines.
winning: not easy.

Ventrue

from watchers that do not see.
I know where you are.

Caitiff

Shifting and sensing.
There may be strength in numbers.
Beware the lucky blow.

Obfuscate

Standing in plain sight,
I work amidst the watchers.
Unseen, I depart.

FYI ;)
A haiku is an impersonal poem, at least at the first level of reading . It
doesn't have a personal involvement. Nor does it express personal feeling,
mood, satire, mockery.
For that, there is the senryuu.
Formally it is a poem with the same metric features as a haiku.

It differs however from a haiku in that:

-- it lacks the mandatory word referring to the season
--it may use humor, subjects from everyday life, business, politics, love
life or sensual ones
--it is often bawdy, even crude
--the poet is involved by describing himself and stating his opinions

The demarcation line between haiku and senryuu is fluid. A slight change in
the expression can move, within the same content, the haiku from one genre
to the other.

Many of the contemporary haiku are in fact senryuu.
